content.title: About
content.content: Kung Pao Beef is a Sichuan Chinese dish featuring tender strips of beef stir‑fried with peanuts, vegetables, and a flavorful sauce made from soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. The dish balances spicy, slightly sweet and nutty notes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Chinese words “Kung” (pepper) and “Pao” (stir‑fry).
While traditional recipes use beef, many variations use chicken, pork or tofu.
Sichuan peppercorn creates a characteristic “numbing” sensation on the palate.
Peanuts are added at the end of cooking to keep them crunchy.
The dish is commonly served with rice or noodles to temper the heat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beef supports hemoglobin levels and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies B12, B6 and niacin, important for metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Sichuan pepper and ginger contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Healthy fats from peanuts
items.content: Peanuts add monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the peanuts used in the dish.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce contributes a significant amount of salt; people monitoring sodium intake should consume in moderation.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Sichuan pepper and dried chilies make the dish very hot; those with sensitive stomachs may want to reduce the spice level.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Peanuts and cooking oil increase the calorie count of the dish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Kung Pao Beef hot, typically over steamed rice or noodles. Fresh vegetables such as bell pepper or green onions can be added for extra crunch and color.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of oil to restore the peanuts’ crispness.
